body:
No cross‑platform arbitrage turned up in today's scan: the scanner checked all live gold contracts across Kalshi and Polymarket and returned zero opportunities. That's the normal, unexciting outcome — most scans come back empty — and today is no different.

The two venues broadly agree on where gold sits right now. On Kalshi, the year‑end settle above ladder crosses the 50-cent mark (where buyers and sellers are evenly split) around the $4,300–$4,400 strikes, and the August 31 settle ladder shows the same crossover near $4,330–$4,370. A settle market like this pays out only on the official price print at a fixed future date. Polymarket's touch contracts, which pay out if price crosses a level at any point during the window rather than only at expiry, tell a consistent story: the $4,350 weekly low-touch trades at 64–73 cents and the $4,450 weekly high-touch trades at 53–57 cents — both priced above even odds in the same week. That isn't a mispricing; it just means traders expect this week's range to be wide enough to tag both a lower and a higher barrier, which is a statement about expected volatility, not a free-money gap between the two platforms.

That elevated volatility fits the backdrop. Gold's run has been historic, with one price tracker noting the record for the highest gold price was set in January 2026, when the metal reached over $5,600 per troy ounce. The same source puts the current price around $4,000, still a nominal record even after the inflation-adjusted 1980 peak was surpassed, consistent with the mid-$4,000s levels implied by today's contracts. Nothing here should be read as a trading signal, just a snapshot of where the two markets currently agree.
headline: Gold scan finds zero cross-platform arbitrage; Kalshi and Polymarket prices align
